approval.comment: Approved v1. classify-v2 draft; I removed one neutral and one label-inconsistent quote (also from R2) and checked the remaining quotes against their answers. The comparison with the approved v1 report shows the method change explains the lower recommended rate; negative and entity-confusion changes are within uncertainty. The analyst notes disclose the method change, the uncertain negative count (holdout2 precision 3/6) and the misattribution advisory. One historical snapshot; citation support not verified.

content.analyst_notes: 1) Method: labels come from classify-v2, promoted on 29 Oct 2026 after evaluation (EVALUATION.md). On the independent holdout2 set it cut "recommended" false positives from 10 to 2 compared with classify-v1, which produced the approved report 7d80ca70. Rates are therefore not comparable with that report: recommended 12/149 vs 40/148 and negative 23/149 vs 30/148 mainly reflect the method change, not a change in the engines' answers (same 31 Jul 2026 capture); only the recommended change lies outside the 95% intervals (report comparison). 2) Entity confusion (9/74 branded answers) is now the third diagnostic. It remains a lower bound: the classifier does not detect product misattribution (evaluation case H06); a separate advisory (claims-v1) flags 2 Kasparro prices cited only to other sites, which are not counted. 3) The negative count is uncertain: on holdout2, 3 of classify-v2's 6 negative calls matched the human label, so 23/74 may overstate unfavourable framing. Quotes that the human labels treat as neutral or not negative were removed. 4) 1 of 150 answers failed validation (non-verbatim quote) and is excluded from all rates, not scored as zero. 5) A live re-run of 38 labelled cases reproduced every label in at least 37 of 38 cases. All counts come from one historical capture; no causal or ranking claims are made.
